promptText: When an owner wants a collection or soft-brand option for a hotel conversion, which brands are commonly considered globally?
rawText:
When a hotel owner is considering *conversion* into a soft‑brand or collection-brand, they generally seek a balance between retaining the property's unique identity and gaining access to a global distribution and loyalty infrastructure. Here are the most commonly considered soft-brand options globally, organized by parent company:

Hilton Worldwide  
• Curio Collection by Hilton – upper‑upscale, design‑forward soft brand ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  
• Tapestry Collection by Hilton – upscale soft brand, often positioned slightly below Curio ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  
• LXR Hotels & Resorts – positioned at the luxury end; though branded, it's often treated similarly to soft brands in terms of unique, independent identity ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  

Marriott International  
• Autograph Collection – upper‑upscale soft brand launched in 2010 (“Exactly Like Nothing Else”) ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  
• Tribute Portfolio – upscale lifestyle collection started in 2015 ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  
• The Luxury Collection – luxury soft brand, one of the earliest in the industry; strong heritage and converted, iconic properties ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  

Hyatt Hotels  
• Unbound Collection – luxury soft brand focusing on distinctive, design‑rich hotels ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  
• Destination by Hyatt – typically resort‑focused, often group‑oriented properties ([mediapost.com](https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/391394/marketing-branded-hotel-collections-its-a-dance.html?utm_source=openai))  
• JdV by Hyatt (formerly Joie de Vivre Hotels & Resorts) – reflecting local neighborhood character ([cbre.ca](https://www.cbre.ca/insights/briefs/soft-brands-a-third-alternative?utm_source=openai))  

Choice Hotels International  
• Ascend Hotel Collection – the original soft brand, launched in 2008; continues to lead in conversions globally ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascend_Collection?utm_source=openai))  

Wyndham Hotels & Resorts  
• Trademark Collection – upper‑midscale soft‑brand designed for independent, character‑rich hotels ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  
• Registry Collection Hotels – positioned at the luxury end, offering a more upscale soft‑brand alternative ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))  

IHG (InterContinental Hotels Group)  
• voco – soft-brand launched in 2018, upscale to upper‑upscale in positioning ([hotelexecutive.com](https://www.hotelexecutive.com/feature_focus/8278/soft-brands-strong-appeal-how-hotels-are-blending-identity-and-experience?utm_source=openai))  
• Vignette Collection – conversion-oriented and flexible soft‑brand solution ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))  

Best Western  
• BW Premier Collection – upper‑midscale to upscale soft‑brand collection ([joinchoicehotels.com](https://www.joinchoicehotels.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/1457123_Development_WhitePaper_SoftBranding_EMEA.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
• BW Signature Collection – additional soft‑brand tier offering distinctive properties ([joinchoicehotels.com](https://www.joinchoicehotels.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/1457123_Development_WhitePaper_SoftBranding_EMEA.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

Radisson Hotel Group (through Jin Jiang)  
• Radisson Individuals (APAC/EMEA) – flexible soft‑brand focused on conversions ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))  
• Radisson Collection – luxury lifestyle soft‑brand in Europe and beyond ([joinchoicehotels.com](https://www.joinchoicehotels.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/1457123_Development_WhitePaper_SoftBranding_EMEA.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

Other Pre‑Branded/Luxury Collection Options  
• Preferred Hotels & Resorts, Leading Hotels of the World, Small Luxury Hotels of the World – independent soft‑brand affiliations offering distribution and marketing to independent hotels ([costar.com](https://www.costar.com/article/1094160855/what-is-a-soft-brand-and-is-it-of-real-value?utm_source=openai))  

**Summary Table (Global Soft‑Brand Options)**  
- Hilton: Curio, Tapestry, LXR  
- Marriott: Autograph, Tribute, Luxury Collection  
- Hyatt: Unbound, Destination, JdV by Hyatt  
- Choice: Ascend Collection  
- Wyndham: Trademark Collection, Registry Collection  
- IHG: voco, Vignette Collection  
- Best Western: Premier Collection, Signature Collection  
- Radisson (Jin Jiang): Radisson Individuals, Radisson Collection  
- Independent Affiliations: Preferred Hotels, Leading Hotels of the World, SLH  

These soft‑brand options are especially attractive in *conversion scenarios*, where the existing building may not meet the compliance requirements of a hard brand but has character and market appeal that can flourish under a soft‑brand affiliation ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)).

Let me know if you'd like details on specific brand requirements, regional availability, or how these brands compare in terms of fees or support for owners.
